name: Camp de la Bóta memorial (Fraternitat)
story: The Camp de la Bóta, an old military ground on the shore at the edge of Barcelona, was the main execution site of Francoist repression in the city. It had already been used by the Republican side in 1936 for executions of people convicted of taking part in the military rising. Between 1939 and 1952, 1,686 people were shot here after court-martial, according to the figure the Generalitat uses for its new memorial. Most were buried in the Fossar de la Pedrera. The 'Fraternitat' monument by Miquel Navarro, erected in 1992, remembers them, and the Generalitat's memorial 'Bosc d'Empremtes' has one iron tube for each person shot.
see: A tall modern sculpture near the Fòrum esplanade, with a plaque; nothing survives of the camp itself.
plan: Beside the Ronda Litoral near the Fòrum; free; tram T4 or metro L4 (El Maresme | Fòrum).

boxes.text: Counts differ because the registers and the areas counted differ: the Generalitat uses 1,686 (1939–52), the older plaque gives 1,734, and other studies give 1,717 executions in Barcelona for 1939–52. Executions here by the Republican side in 1936 are not well documented.
